Analytical assessment · grade D

Accession forecast

The working horizon is 2027. The forecast depends on closing the action plans, border-control arrangements and agreement between member states.

Accelerated scenario

By 1 July 2027

This requires prompt closure of the action plans, agreement on special arrangements, consultation of the European Parliament and a unanimous Council decision.

Confidence in an exact date is low.

Working scenario

During 2027

The procedures could be completed within the year if member states agree on border checks and avoid a prolonged deadlock.

Confidence in the year-long horizon is moderate.

If delayed

Late 2027 and beyond

Protracted legal or political disagreements could push accession to late 2027, 2028 or later.

Fallback scenario.

What could change the forecast

Closing six action plans

The draft covers data protection, return, external borders, police cooperation, visas and SIS. A published closure decision would clarify which technical conditions have been met.

Council of the EU · draft ST 14872/26 Council of the EU · agenda CM 4752/1/26 REV 1

The Green Line and the bases

Entry and exit records must be agreed in light of the Green Line's special status, alongside checks at the British base crossings. The EU and UK have reaffirmed their work on the protocol.

EUR-Lex · Regulation (EU) 2024/1356 Council of the EU · ST 16174/26, point 5 Politis · checks at two crossings

Airport readiness

The impact of the Paphos and Larnaca tender on the July target depends on whether the new booths must be operational before full application of the rules.

Cyprus eProcurement · MTCW/AIR2/BOOTHS/2026 Phileleftheros · airport equipment

The political decision

Greece's support helps negotiations. A Council act, following consultation of the European Parliament, will determine the date and scope of full application.

Greek Prime Minister · Nicosia transcript Cyprus Act of Accession · Article 3(2)
